starts tune A: for each voice, the track the tune gives it ($29EE), its data pointer ($A0-$A5) and a wait of one frame ($C1-$C3); a voice whose entry is $FF is left as it is. The processor's interrupt flag is kept
builds the music's frequency table at $C000: eight octaves of twelve notes, 192 bytes, each octave the top one ($286A) shifted right, note n at $C000 + 2n; then silences the SID ($2458)
silences the music: clears the SID's registers ($D401 on) and the driver's variables ($A0-$DF), and sets the pulse sweep's start to $0400

plays one frame of music, from the raster interrupt. For each voice, 3 down to 1: when the note's frames run out the gate is let go, unless held, and the next commands and note are read ($2493); then the pulse width sweep for the voices that have it ($CC), up and down between $0200 and $0E00 by $0F a frame, or $10 when the carry is left set (nothing clears it before the addition), and the vibrato for those that have it ($D2), each voice's frequency moved up or down by its step and turned round after its period
reads the voice's next byte: $EA is skipped, $FF ends the voice (pointer cleared, gate off), below $C0 a note ($27BA), otherwise a command from the table at $2828
the next voice
the pulse width, the same for every voice that sweeps

the vibrato: every voice in $D2 counts its period down ($D9) and turns its direction round (bit 7 of $D4) when it runs out, adding or subtracting the step to its frequency; then the three frequencies are written to the SID
the offset of each voice's registers from $D400: 0, 7 and 14
command $C1: the voice's frequency, two bytes, straight to the SID
command $DD: a pulse wave ($40) with the pulse width at $0800
command $C2: the voice's waveform (its control register without the gate), one byte
command $C3: the voice's pulse width, two bytes
command $C4: the voice's envelope, attack-decay then sustain-release
command $C5: the filter's cutoff, low then high byte
command $C9: lowers the filter's cutoff by a byte, then reads a length as a note does
command $D6: raises the filter's cutoff by a byte, then a length
command $C6: the filter's resonance, the high nibble of a byte
command $C0: adds a byte to the volume, the result kept below 16
command $C7: the volume, the low nibble of a byte, with the filter type kept
command $C8: a wait: the voice reads nothing more for that many frames
command $CA: puts the voice through the filter
command $CB: the filter type, the high nibble of a byte, with the volume kept
command $CC: takes the voice out of the filter
command $CD: sets the voice's first repeat count ($B7)

command $D2: the second repeat, as $CE with the count at $B4
command $DA: lowers the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $CF: lowers the frequency by a byte, then a length

command $D0: raises the frequency by a byte, then a length

command $DC: vibrato off for the voice

command $D4: pulse width sweep off for the voice
